newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon charges Japanese Red Army suspects.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon charges Japanese Red Army suspects.

text.p: Lebanon said on Thursday it was not concerned whether five Japanese Red Army suspects it holds belonged to the international guerrilla group and confirmed it was charging them for offences against its laws.
"This is not our business," Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum told reporters when asked if Lebanon had identified the five as Japanese Red Army members.

Addoum said Beirut Prosecutor Abdallah Bitar charged the five with possessing and using forged passports, forging Lebanese government official stamps, entering the country illegally and illegal residence.
"The articles under which all the accused are charged carry penalties up to seven years hard labour," Addoum said.
The Lebanese decision appeared to put an end to Tokyo's hopes of quickly extraditing them to stand trial for international offences.
Addoum said the Lebanese judiciary had made no deal with Japan on the fate of the five suspected guerrillas or three other Japanese citizens who were detained with them but were released later.

He denied the three had been handed over to Japanese security agents who arrived in Lebanon after the eight were arrested on February 15. He said the Lebanese judiciary had found that the three had no links with Japanese intelligence.
"Lebanese judicial authorities do not make any deal with any state, and Japan is not a party to the case, so why should we hand the released people to the Japanese?" he told reporters.

Japan originally hoped Lebanon would quickly deport the five to face trial in Japan, but the case became bogged down in confusion for nearly three weeks before Beirut decided to try them for local offences.

The case will now be handed to an investigative judge who will carry out investigations and either order the suspects to be tried or released, depending on whether there is sufficient evidence of guilt, judicial sources added.
Addoum identified the five accused as Kozo Okamoto, Masao Adachi, Mariko Yamamoto, Kazuo Tohira and Haruo Wako. Japan says these are the names of Japanese Red Army guerrillas.
The three who were released were identified as Sei Harada, Moroshima Takayaki and Shamato Yushiyoki.
Japanese officials briefly met the detainees on Wednesday for the first time since they were arrested but were not allowed to interrogate them.
The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. All five suspects are on the international wanted list on various charges.
